fable-fusion-27b.note: Community merge (DavidAU Fable-Fusion-711, dense 27B, uncensored/abliterated), not an official Qwen release. Now used for Open WebUI chat + custom Tools (data fetch/analysis), not coding. Tested: tool-calling works (stream+non-stream), MTP draft acceptance ~78-86%, but raw speed is only ~26 tok/s vs ~74 tok/s on qwen3.6-mtp (dense 27B costs far more per token than the sparse 35B-A3B MoE despite fewer total params). Context ceiling tested by hand: 65536 fits safely (~4.8GB headroom), 98304 triggered an internal CUDA OOM once (auto-recovered by retrying without pipeline parallelism, but left under 800MB free on one card) - not safe for real use, pinned to 65536 instead of trusting --fit's over-conservative 8192 default. Stress-tested tool-calling at temp=1.0 with a tight 400-token budget: 5/5 succeeded (unlike qwen3.6-mtp, which had real failures at its default temp before being lowered to 0.6) - so temperature was NOT overridden here, it's genuinely reliable as-is. --reasoning-budget/--no-reasoning-preserve added anyway as cheap insurance for long chat sessions, same reasoning as the coding profiles. Vision added afterward: unlike the original Unsloth qwen3.6-mtp model (whose card explicitly says MTP + --mmproj aren't supported together, why qwen3.6-main/qwen3.6-mtp are split), this DavidAU merge loads BOTH --spec-type draft-mtp and --mmproj together with no conflict - verified: vision test image correctly described AND MTP draft acceptance still ~82% simultaneously. VRAM headroom is tighter with vision loaded (~28.5GB/32GB used, ~3.8GB free) but stable, no OOM.

muse-glimmer-30b.note: Official Meta Superintelligence Lab release, dense 29.6B with a ViT-G/14 perception encoder, purpose-built for local agentic tasks - not a Qwen derivative. Needed a llama.cpp upgrade to load at all: the 'muse-glimmer' architecture wasn't recognized on b10155 (this model card's release date is Aug 2026, support merged into llama.cpp on 2026-08-10, PR #26841) - upgraded to b10355 to get it. Uses DFlash speculative decoding (block-of-16 drafter, separate --spec-draft-model file) instead of MTP, confirmed active via 'adding speculative implementation draft-dflash' in the log. Controls reasoning depth via a 'Reasoning strength: <low|medium|high|xhigh>' line in the system prompt rather than a CLI flag, so --reasoning-budget/--no-reasoning-preserve were deliberately not copied from other profiles. TESTED RESULTS: tool-calling reliable (8/8 across two batches, including a tight 400-token stress test - no reasoning-runaway issue). Vision works (mmproj loads fine alongside DFlash, no MTP-style conflict). But raw speed is only ~30-34 tok/s with DFlash active - SLOWER than qwen3.6-mtp's ~72-74 tok/s, and nowhere near the model card's claimed 3.1x/233 tok/s DFlash speedup, which was measured on an RTX 5090 (far more compute than this RTX 5060 Ti x2 setup) - marketing numbers from different hardware class did not transfer. --fit auto-picked only 8192 ctx despite ~12GB VRAM headroom being free; tested by hand instead: 131072 (matching the other main profiles) fits comfortably with ~10.3GB headroom to spare, thanks to the model's sliding-window attention (only 1 layer in 4 is 'Global', rest are 2048-window local) costing far less than Fable-Fusion's fully dense attention did. Benchmarks on the model card compare against Qwen3.6-27B specifically (not the 35B-A3B-MoE this setup actually runs day to day) with mixed results - wins agentic/tool benchmarks like MCP Atlas, loses coding-specific ones like TerminalBench/OSWorld/SWE-Bench Verified. Net: works correctly, but not faster than the current setup on this hardware - kept as a profile to try for its native tool-recovery/reasoning-strength design, not adopted as default.
